title: rorca-ux-overhaul
description: Complete UX overhaul: workspace auto-bootstrap, Forge redesign (brief-first minimal), kill L1-L5 jargon (Standards/Conventions/Project), sidebar simplification, merge Review Queue into Forge, fix broken Context Used tab, remove stale internal text, auto-populate direction on workspace add, eliminate Settings double-sidebar and navigation redundancies. 15 stories that make Rorca usable by humans.

userStories.title: Workspace Bootstrap Orchestrator
userStories.description: As the system, I need a single backend endpoint that chains all workspace intelligence into one call — so the frontend can set up a workspace in one request instead of requiring the user to manually configure direction layers, scopes, and context files.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/workspaces/:id/bootstrap endpoint created in backend/src/routes/workspaces.ts

Endpoint chains in order: (1) echolocate(path) to detect stack, monorepo, context files; (2) discoverMonorepo() if monorepo structure found; (3) scan-direction logic to generate L1/L2/L3 content from codebase analysis via LLM; (4) generate .rorca/config.json with globals (CLAUDE.md, MEMORY.md) and scopes (one per detected surface/app); (5) inferSkillsFromStack() to suggest skills per surface; (6) initialize MEMORY.md if missing

Response shape: { surfaces: Array<{ path, name, stack, suggestedL2 }>, direction: { standards, conventions, project }, scopes: Array<{ path, inject, priority }>, suggestedSkills: string[], healthBefore: number, healthAfter: number, filesCreated: string[] }
If workspace already has .rorca/config.json, endpoint returns existing config with a 'configured: true' flag instead of overwriting
If echolocate finds no recognizable stack (empty directory), returns { surfaces: [], direction: { standards: defaultL1, conventions: '', project: '' } } with a flag 'empty: true'
Endpoint completes in < 15 seconds for a typical project (< 1000 files). LLM calls for direction generation are the bottleneck — timeout at 30s with partial results returned
All @swagger annotations present for auto-MCP tool generation
Backend TypeScript compiles with no errors

userStories.title: First-Run Workspace Wizard
userStories.description: As a new user who just added a workspace, I want Rorca to automatically scan my project and set everything up in one click — so I never have to manually configure direction layers, scopes, or context files.
acceptanceCriteria: When a workspace is added (via Add Workspace or first load) AND the workspace health score is below 40% (from echolocate), the Workspace Wizard appears as a full-screen overlay instead of the blank Hub

Step 1 — 'Scanning your project...': animated progress bar, text updates showing what's being scanned ('Reading package.json...', 'Analyzing directory structure...', 'Detecting tech stack...'). Calls POST /api/workspaces/:id/bootstrap

Step 2 — 'Here's what I found': card per detected surface (e.g., 'website/' → Next.js 14, Tailwind; 'src/' → React 18, Vite; 'backend/' → Express, SQLite). Each card shows: directory path, detected stack badges, what context will be configured. User can remove a surface card (click X) or rename it. Expandable 'Show details' on each card reveals the generated direction text

Step 3 — 'Ready to go': summary ('3 surfaces configured, Standards + Conventions + Project populated, Memory initialized'). Primary button: 'Start Building' (navigates to Forge). Secondary link: 'Customize in Settings' (for power users)
Clicking 'Start Building' saves all generated config (direction layers written to DB, .rorca/config.json written to disk, MEMORY.md initialized if missing) and navigates to Forge

If bootstrap returns 'empty: true' (no detectable stack), wizard shows: 'I couldn't detect a stack. Tell me about your project:' with a brief textarea → generates direction from user description instead of codebase scan
Wizard is dismissible (X button top right) — drops user to Hub with a persistent banner: 'Finish setting up your workspace' that re-opens the wizard
Wizard does NOT appear for workspaces with health score >= 40% (already configured)
Frontend TypeScript compiles with no errors

userStories.title: Forge Redesign — Brief-First Minimal
userStories.description: As a user, I want the Forge to be a simple brief input with two buttons — so I can go from idea to spec without navigating a complex three-column layout full of jargon I don't understand.
acceptanceCriteria: Forge layout changed from three-column to single-column centered (max-w-2xl mx-auto)

Primary view shows ONLY: (1) large brief textarea with placeholder 'What do you want to build?' (min 6 rows, auto-expands), (2) context health indicator below textarea — three small dots labeled 'Standards', 'Conventions', 'Project' with green fill when populated, grey when empty, (3) two buttons: 'Generate Spec' (primary) and 'Quick Run' (secondary, outline)

Remove from primary view: token/char counter ('~2 tokens 5 chars' at SpecForgePanelPage.tsx:429-441 — delete entirely, not hide), Direction Context side panel (the L1/L2/L3 readout currently in center column), Save/Export/Ralph Loop panel (entire right column from SpecForgeOutput.tsx SaveTab)

Context health dots are clickable — clicking an empty (grey) dot opens a small inline popover: 'Standards not configured — [Set up now]' which either opens the wizard (UX-002) or an inline textarea for quick entry

'Advanced Options' toggle still exists but is collapsed by default and moved BELOW the Generate button — not between brief and button. Contains: spec name override, model selector, story count, workspace selector. Remove 'Direction Stack Overrides' section entirely (L4/L5 fields at SpecForgePanelPage.tsx:566-590 — delete). Remove Domain field. Remove story prefix field. Remove diagram checkbox. Remove 6-pass pipeline checkbox. Remove output format selector
Single/Batch toggle at top right of page remains (some users need batch)
'Start from template' link remains above the brief textarea
Frontend TypeScript compiles with no errors

userStories.title: Forge Redesign — Post-Generate Flow
userStories.description: As a user who just generated a spec, I want to see my stories and approve+run in one click — without navigating tabs for Save, Context Used, Diagrams, or Copy PRD JSON.
acceptanceCriteria: After spec generation completes, the brief textarea collapses to a single line showing the brief text (click to expand and edit), and the generated spec appears below it in the same view
Generated spec view shows: spec name (editable inline), story count badge, list of stories with title + description preview (2 lines) + checkbox to include/exclude each story

Primary action bar at bottom: 'Approve & Run' button (large, primary — combines approve + trigger pipeline in one click, opens workspace selector + auto-worktree toggle dialog, then triggers), 'Approve' button (secondary — approves without running), 'Reject' button (tertiary, text-only, red — deletes spec with confirmation)

Remove from post-generate view: the 4-tab bar (Stories / Diagram / Save / Context Used) from SpecForgeOutput.tsx. Stories are shown inline (not in a tab). Diagram is accessible via a small 'View diagram' link below the story list, not a top-level tab. Save tab removed entirely (the 'Save Spec to Workspace' button, spec file destination path, Copy PRD JSON, Ralph Loop stub — all deleted from SpecForgeOutput.tsx:300-435). Context Used tab removed (moved to UX-012 fix)
The 'Approve & Run' flow: click → dialog shows workspace selector + 'Run in worktree' toggle → confirm → spec approved + pipeline triggered → navigate to Pipeline Monitor automatically
After approval, the Forge resets to the empty brief state with a success toast: 'Spec approved — running now' (if Approve & Run) or 'Spec approved — ready to run from Pipeline' (if Approve only)
Frontend TypeScript compiles with no errors

userStories.title: Kill L1-L5 Naming Everywhere
userStories.description: As a user, I want to see 'Standards', 'Conventions', and 'Project' instead of 'L1', 'L2', 'L3' — because layer numbers mean nothing to me.
acceptanceCriteria: SettingsPanel.tsx LAYER_INFO (line 85-101): 'L1 — Global Standards' → 'Standards', 'L2 — Domain Knowledge' → 'Conventions', 'L3 — Project Context' → 'Project'. Descriptions stay the same
DirectionStackPanel.tsx SIMPLE_LABELS (line 30-46): 'Global Standards' → 'Standards', 'Domain Knowledge' → 'Conventions', 'Project Context' → 'Project'
DirectionStackPanel.tsx ADVANCED labels: 'L1 Global Brain' → 'Standards', 'L2 Domain Profile' → 'Conventions', 'L3 Project Brief' → 'Project'

SpecForgePanelPage.tsx Direction Context sidebar (the middle column, which UX-003 moves to health dots): labels 'L1 — Global', 'L2 — Domain', 'L3 — Project' → 'Standards', 'Conventions', 'Project' (in the health dot popovers)
TeamDirectionPanel.tsx: 'L1 Team Standards' → 'Team Standards', 'L2 Team Domain Profile' → 'Team Conventions'

Remove ALL instances of 'L4' and 'L5' from user-facing UI. These are internal concepts (spec brief and story annotations are auto-populated). Grep for 'L4' and 'L5' in src/ — every match in a label, placeholder, heading, or description must be removed or reworded

Remove ALL instances of 'Direction Stack' as a user-facing term in headings and navigation labels. Replace with 'Direction' (shorter, less jargony). The sidebar item 'Direction Stack' → 'Direction'. The settings tab 'Direction Stack' → 'Direction'. The panel heading 'Direction Stack Composer' → 'Direction'

Tooltip help text updated: 'Standards' → 'How you build software — engineering principles that apply to all projects', 'Conventions' → 'Patterns for this type of project — framework and domain conventions', 'Project' → 'What makes this project unique — its stack, architecture, and constraints'
The cascade rule explained in plain English wherever layers are shown: 'Project beats Conventions beats Standards' (small text, like a footer note in the direction editor)
Frontend TypeScript compiles with no errors

userStories.title: Sidebar Simplification
userStories.description: As a new user, I want to see 5 navigation items instead of 24 — so I can find what I need without scanning a wall of links I don't understand.
acceptanceCriteria: NAV_SECTIONS in Sidebar.tsx reduced from 5 sections / 24 items to a flat list of top-level items: 'Forge' (Wand2 icon), 'Runs' (Activity icon — replaces 'Monitor'), 'Archive' (Archive icon), 'Direction' (Layers icon), 'Settings' (Settings icon)
'+ New Spec' shortcut at top of sidebar remains — navigates to Forge
Workspace selector dropdown at top of sidebar remains
Search / Command Palette (Cmd+K) at top remains

Removed from top-level sidebar: Review Queue (merged into Forge per UX-007), Templates/Marketplace (moved to a tab within Archive or a section in Forge 'Start from template'), Worktrees (moved to a tab within Runs), Compare Runs (moved to a tab within Runs), Team Direction (moved to a tab within Direction), Memory Ledger (moved to a tab within Direction), ALL analytics items (Token Usage, Cost Breakdown, Model Comparison, Velocity Chart, Completion Rates, ROI Calculator, FinOps, Health — all moved behind a single 'Analytics' tab within Settings or a dedicated 'Analytics' sub-page accessible from Settings)
Direction panel gets tabs: 'Standards / Conventions / Project' (the 3 layers) + 'Memory' + 'Rules' (the power-user scope config from ContextRoutingSettings, previously buried in Settings)
Runs panel gets tabs: 'Active' (current Pipeline Monitor view) + 'History' (previous runs list) + 'Worktrees' + 'Compare'
Settings panel gets sections: 'Account', 'Providers' (model selection, API keys), 'GitHub', 'Analytics' (all 8 analytics panels accessible from here as sub-tabs), 'Billing'
All PanelId types preserved for deep linking and Command Palette — sidebar just doesn't render them all as top-level items
Command Palette (Cmd+K) can still reach every panel by name (even ones not in sidebar) — 'Token Usage', 'Velocity Chart', etc. still work as command palette targets
Frontend TypeScript compiles with no errors

userStories.title: Merge Review Queue into Forge
userStories.description: As a user, I want pending specs to appear in Forge instead of a separate Review Queue panel — because having two places to manage specs is confusing and I don't understand what 'Review Queue' means.
acceptanceCriteria: Review Queue removed from sidebar (per UX-006)

Forge panel now has two states: (1) 'Create' — the brief input (UX-003), shown when no pending specs exist OR when user clicks '+ New Spec'; (2) 'Pending' — list of pending specs awaiting review, shown when pending specs exist

When pending specs exist, Forge shows a spec list above the brief input area: each spec card shows name, story count, generated timestamp, status badge (Draft / Needs Review). Click a spec card → expands to show story list with inline approve/reject actions (same approve/reject UX from ReviewQueuePanel but rendered inline in Forge)
The brief input is always visible at the top (maybe collapsed to a single-line '+ New Spec' when viewing a pending spec, expandable on click)

All Review Queue functionality preserved: story editing, story comments, dependency graph (accessible via 'View graph' link), approval with hotkeys (Cmd+Enter to approve, Cmd+Backspace to reject), reject with reason textarea
ReviewQueuePanel.tsx is deleted. Its components (InlineStoryEditor, StoryComments, DependencyGraph, SpecConfirmDialog) are moved to shared components or imported directly by Forge
The 'queue' PanelId still works in Command Palette and deep links — it navigates to Forge with the pending specs view visible
Frontend TypeScript compiles with no errors

userStories.title: Context Health Indicator
userStories.description: As a user writing a spec brief, I want to see at a glance whether my workspace has good context — and fix it inline without navigating to Settings.
acceptanceCriteria: Below the brief textarea in Forge, a horizontal row of 3 small indicators: 'Standards' dot, 'Conventions' dot, 'Project' dot
Each dot is a 6px circle: filled green (var(--accent) or emerald) when the corresponding direction layer has content (non-empty string in direction_layers DB), filled grey (var(--border)) when empty
Next to each dot, the label in text-xs text-muted: 'Standards', 'Conventions', 'Project'

Clicking an empty (grey) indicator opens a popover anchored to that dot: heading 'Conventions not configured' (or whichever layer), description 'Patterns for this type of project — detected from your codebase or entered manually', two options: 'Auto-detect' button (runs the scan-direction logic for that layer only) and a textarea for manual entry with 'Save' button
Clicking a green (filled) indicator opens a popover showing a preview of the layer content (first 200 chars with 'View full' link that navigates to Direction panel)
Direction layer state fetched from GET /api/direction on Forge mount — cached, not re-fetched on every render
If ALL three dots are grey, show a subtle banner above the dots: 'No direction configured yet — your specs will be better with context. [Set up now]' linking to the wizard (UX-002) or Direction panel
Frontend TypeScript compiles with no errors

userStories.title: Remove Stale and Internal Text
userStories.description: As a user, I want the UI to never show internal developer terminology, stale phase references, or debug information — because it makes the product feel unfinished.
acceptanceCriteria: SpecForgeOutput.tsx: delete the entire 'Ralph stub' section (lines 422-435): the 'Run in Ralph Loop' heading, 'Connect to Pipeline Monitor' disabled button, and 'Coming in Phase 3' text. This section is dead code — pipeline triggering is handled by the Approve & Run flow (UX-004)

SpecForgePanelPage.tsx: delete the token/char counter below the brief textarea (lines 429-441). Users don't need to know their brief is '~2 tokens 5 chars'. If a brief length warning is needed, show it only when the brief exceeds 3000 chars as a simple 'Brief is getting long — consider splitting into multiple specs'

SpecForgeOutput.tsx: delete the SPEC FILE DESTINATION display (lines 370-376) showing the raw filesystem path. Users don't need to see '/Users/dimitri/workspace/specs/undefined.json'. The system handles file paths internally
SpecForgeOutput.tsx: delete the 'Copy PRD JSON' export button (line 385-395). If JSON export is needed, it belongs in Archive (where completed specs live), not in the generation flow

SpecForgePanelPage.tsx: delete the 'Direction Stack Overrides' section header (line 568) and the L4/L5 textarea fields (lines 569-590). L4 is auto-populated from the brief. L5 is auto-populated by the generation pipeline. Users never need to manually type these

Grep entire src/ directory for: 'Ralph', 'Phase 3', 'Phase 2', 'Phase 1' (as user-facing strings, not code comments). Remove or replace every instance. 'Ralph Loop' → 'Pipeline'. 'Phase N' → remove entirely
Grep entire src/ directory for: 'L4', 'L5' as visible text in JSX (not variable names). Remove every user-facing instance
Grep entire src/ directory for: 'Direction Stack' as a heading or label (not code comments). Replace with 'Direction' everywhere
Frontend TypeScript compiles with no errors

userStories.title: Auto-Bootstrap on Workspace Add
userStories.description: As a user adding a new workspace, I want Rorca to automatically scan and configure it — so I never land on a blank page with 'Not configured' labels and no guidance on what to do.
acceptanceCriteria: When POST /api/workspaces creates a new workspace, the response includes a 'needsBootstrap: true' flag if the workspace health score (from echolocate) is below 40%
Frontend workspace creation flow (wherever 'Add Workspace' lives): after successful creation, if needsBootstrap is true, automatically navigate to the Workspace Wizard (UX-002) instead of the Hub

If the user switches to a workspace that has health < 40% and has never been bootstrapped (no .rorca/config.json exists), show a non-blocking banner at top of whatever panel they're on: 'This workspace isn't set up yet — your specs will work better with context. [Set up now]' → opens wizard
Banner is dismissible (X button). Once dismissed, it doesn't reappear for that workspace in the current session. Dismissal stored in localStorage per workspace ID
The Hub/Overview panel for an unconfigured workspace shows the wizard prompt prominently — not just a blank page with empty data
Workspaces that already have .rorca/config.json OR health >= 40% never see the wizard or banner — they go directly to the Hub as normal
Frontend TypeScript compiles with no errors

userStories.title: Settings Simplification
userStories.description: As a user, I want Settings to show me the things I actually need (account, model, API keys) — not a power-user config panel for token budgets, priority sliders, and JSON editors.
acceptanceCriteria: Settings panel restructured into clear sections: 'Account' (user profile, password, preferences), 'Providers' (execution engine selector: Claude/OpenCode/Codex, model dropdown, API key vault entries), 'GitHub' (connection status, OAuth), 'Billing' (plan, quotas, upgrade)

ContextRoutingSettings (the Rules Engine — scope rules, directory tree, priority sliders, token budget, JSON editor) moved INSIDE the Direction panel as a 'Rules' tab (per UX-006) — NOT in Settings. This is a direction/context configuration concern, not a settings concern

Analytics panels (Token Usage, Cost Breakdown, Model Comparison, Velocity Chart, Completion Rates, ROI Calculator, FinOps, Health) accessible from Settings via an 'Analytics' section that renders the selected analytics panel inline — or from Command Palette by name. They are NOT top-level sidebar items
Settings no longer shows direction layer editors (L1/L2/L3 textareas). Direction editing lives in the Direction panel exclusively — one canonical location, not two
System panels (Audit Log, Activity Feed) accessible from Settings via a 'System' section or from Command Palette. NOT top-level sidebar items
Settings panel code size reduced — SettingsPanel.tsx delegates to sub-components (this aligns with PR-029 from the production-ready spec if it runs first, but this story is self-contained)
Frontend TypeScript compiles with no errors

userStories.title: Fix Context Used — Show What Was Injected
userStories.description: As a user who generated a spec, I want to see exactly what context was injected into the generation — so I can debug why a spec came out wrong or verify my direction layers were used.
acceptanceCriteria: Backend: POST /api/specs/generate response now includes a 'contextUsed' field containing the full synthesized direction text that was sent to the LLM. This is the output of synthesize() + any scoped context from the routing system

Backend: contextUsed also includes metadata: { standards: boolean, conventions: boolean, project: boolean, memory: boolean, scopesMatched: string[], totalTokens: number } — showing which layers contributed and how many tokens were used

Frontend: instead of the removed 'Context Used' tab (UX-004 removed the tab bar), context info is accessible via a small 'Context injected' link below the generated spec in Forge. Clicking it expands an inline panel showing: which layers were active (Standards checkmark, Conventions checkmark, Project X), total tokens injected, and expandable full text
If contextUsed is empty (no direction configured), the link text changes to 'No context injected — set up direction to improve spec quality' with a link to Direction panel
The contextUsed field is stored alongside the spec in the database (or in the spec JSON itself) so it's available after navigating away and coming back
Backend TypeScript compiles with no errors
Frontend TypeScript compiles with no errors

userStories.title: Kill the Double Sidebar in Settings
userStories.description: As a user, I want one settings navigation — not two competing sidebars on the same screen that show overlapping items and contradict each other on whether I'm editing 'my account' or 'workspace settings'.
acceptanceCriteria: The current SettingsSidebar (left sidebar with 'YOUR ACCOUNT': Direction Stack, Model & Providers, GitHub, Personas, Shortcuts, Account, Billing) and the WorkspaceSettings inner sidebar (General, Direction Stack, Workspace Context, GitHub, Env Vars, Pipeline, Hooks, Agents) are MERGED into a single settings navigation

Single settings sidebar with two clear sections: 'WORKSPACE' (General, Direction, Providers, GitHub, Env Vars, Pipeline, Hooks, Agents) and 'ACCOUNT' (Shortcuts, Account, Billing). Section headers clearly distinguish workspace-scoped vs user-scoped settings
Remove the 'YOUR ACCOUNT' header from the left sidebar — it's misleading because Direction Stack and Model & Providers are workspace settings, not account settings

'Direction Stack' appears exactly ONCE in the settings sidebar — not in both the left sidebar AND the inner sidebar. The workspace Direction Stack and the account Direction Stack are the same editor, not two different views
'GitHub' appears exactly ONCE — not in both sidebars. Workspace GitHub connection and account GitHub are the same thing

The heading 'Workspace Settings' at top of the content area stays — it correctly describes what this page is. But the left sidebar stops calling itself 'YOUR ACCOUNT' when half its items are workspace settings
When clicking 'Settings' from the main sidebar (UX-006), user lands on a single settings page with one sidebar. No 'Workspace Settings' as a separate sub-destination within settings
The 'Back to Rorca' button at top of settings sidebar remains — it exits the settings context back to the main app
Frontend TypeScript compiles with no errors

userStories.title: Eliminate Navigation Redundancies
userStories.description: As a user, I want every navigation item to go to a unique destination — no two buttons that do the same thing.
acceptanceCriteria: '+ New Spec' button in sidebar and 'Forge' sidebar item: '+ New Spec' is removed as a separate sidebar item. The 'Forge' item IS the way to create a new spec. If the user is already in Forge viewing a pending spec, clicking 'Forge' in the sidebar scrolls to the brief input at top (same as '+ New Spec' would have done). The '+ New Spec' shortcut can remain as a button INSIDE the Forge panel (above the brief textarea) but not as a top-level sidebar item duplicating Forge

Alternatively if '+ New Spec' is kept as a top-level convenience: it must navigate to Forge AND clear/collapse any pending spec view so the brief input is prominent. It should feel like a 'new document' action, not a navigation to a panel that happens to have an input field

'Workspace Settings' in the main sidebar and the settings inner content: 'Workspace Settings' is removed from the main sidebar as a separate item. Clicking 'Settings' takes you to settings, which includes workspace settings. One entry point, not two
Templates/Marketplace as a sidebar item: removed per UX-006 (moved to be a section within Forge or Archive). But verify there's no other way to reach the same panel from two different sidebar items

Overview/Hub panel: if it shows the same information available from other panels (recent runs = Pipeline Monitor, pending specs = Forge), evaluate whether it should be the default landing page or whether Forge should be the default. If Overview stays, it must add value beyond being a dashboard of links to other panels
Audit all PanelIds in NAV_SECTIONS: no two sidebar items should render the same underlying component or fetch the same data
Frontend TypeScript compiles with no errors

userStories.title: Kill Jargon in Workspace Settings Fields
userStories.description: As a user editing workspace settings, I want field labels and descriptions that make sense to me — not internal implementation terminology.
acceptanceCriteria: Workspace Settings 'Domains' field: label changed from 'Domains' to 'Project Type'. Description changed from 'Comma-separated domain tags for L2 direction matching' to 'What kind of project is this? (e.g., saas, marketing-site, api, cli)'. Remove mention of 'L2' and 'direction matching' — users don't know what those mean

Workspace Settings 'Default Model' description: changed from 'Default LLM model for spec generation in this workspace' to 'Model used when generating specs for this workspace'. Remove 'LLM' — normal users don't know the acronym

Workspace Settings 'Path' description: changed from 'Absolute path to the project workspace. Must exist on filesystem.' to 'Where this project lives on your computer'. Remove 'Absolute path' and 'filesystem' — developer jargon

Workspace Settings 'Workspace ID' field: this is read-only (monospace, grey background). Add a small help text: 'Auto-generated identifier. Used in API calls and file paths.' Or better: hide it entirely behind an 'Advanced' toggle since normal users never need to see it

Any field in any settings panel that references 'L1', 'L2', 'L3', 'direction matching', 'direction layers', 'synthesize', 'routing config', 'token budget', or 'scope rules' in user-facing descriptions must be rewritten in plain English
Frontend TypeScript compiles with no errors
